construct: Acid in the duodenum stimulates S cells to release secretin. Secretin activates basolateral Gs-coupled receptors on pancreatic ductal/centroacinar cells, increasing cAMP and promoting bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion. Apical CFTR is central to ductal chloride/bicarbonate transport and supports highly alkaline pancreatic juice.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Duodenal acid releases secretin, which raises cAMP in pancreatic duct cells and drives bicarbonate-rich secretion; apical CFTR is central to chloride/bicarbonate transport.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Other apical epithelial transporters are physiologically real but do not mediate secretin-stimulated pancreatic ductal bicarbonate secretion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The S-cell hormone, ductal cAMP signal, and bicarbonate-rich pancreatic fluid uniquely identify CFTR.
